triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: Cassava production in Africa occurs within a variety of cropping systems which, on a given parcel of land, could be in the form of:

triples.subject: Monocrop
triples.source_sentence: Monocrop - cassava is the only crop on the plot; this is found mainly on large-scale commercial farms.

triples.subject: Intercrop
triples.source_sentence: Intercrop - cassava is grown alongside other crops on the same plot at the same time.

triples.subject: Crop rotation
triples.source_sentence: Crop rotation - this can take two forms:

triples.subject: Continuous cropping
triples.source_sentence: (1) Crop rotation under continuous cropping: This involves continued use of the same parcel of land while alternating the crops grown from one season to the next or from one year to the next.

triples.subject: Fallow
triples.source_sentence: (2) Crop rotation nested in fallow: Fallow involves leaving a parcel of land unused for some time to enable soil fertility to build back up before reuse.

triples.subject: Natural fallow
triples.source_sentence: Some fallows are natural (i.e. the land is left unsown, as commonly practiced in West and Central Africa)

triples.subject: Managed fallow
triples.source_sentence: while others are managed (i.e. a cover crop is planted on the land to enhance the soil fertility restoration process).

triples.subject: Traditional cropping system
triples.source_sentence: Under the traditional cropping system, which involves growing a mixture of different crops and varieties of crops on the same plot of land at the same time, there is limited scope for the intensification of any one of the crops.

triples.subject: Commercial farms
triples.source_sentence: Monocrop - cassava is the only crop on the plot; this is found mainly on large-scale commercial farms.

triples.subject: cassava mosaic disease (CMD)
triples.source_sentence: Management skills - Minimal skills are needed to select and cut planting sticks and to place these in the soil. However, care should be taken to avoid the spread of diseases like cassava mosaic disease (CMD) and cassava brown streak disease (CBSD). Farmers in areas with CMD and/or CBSD infestation need to select clean planting materials and take care to avoid the use of cutting implements contaminated by the disease.

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: Once the variety to be grown has been selected, the farmer should ensure that the plants from which the cuttings are taken are free of signs of disease, such as cassava mosaic disease and anthracnose, the implements used to cut plants are clean and have not been used on sick plants, and that the cuttings themselves are:

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: clean-cut, not splintered and bark not chipped off (cut with a sharp implement and handle the cuttings with care to avoid damage) (Photo 3)

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: kept upright in the shade with the base partly buried in the soil to avoid drying (if there is need for temporary storage)

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: If there is need to store planting material for a longer time, long stems can be stored upright under a tree, with the bases buried in moist soil.

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: At planting, the top and bottom ends of the stem should be cut off and discarded, the rest of the stem should be cut to the right size for planting.

triples.subject: Cassava

triples.subject: Spacing
triples.source_sentence: The currently recommended spacing is a square arrangement, 1 m x 1 m, i.e. one cassava plant per square metre. This gives 10,000 plants per hectare.

triples.subject: Spacing
triples.object: 1 m x 0.5 m or 1 m x 0.75 m
triples.source_sentence: For varieties that grow upright without branching (as opposed to low and profusely branching varieties), a higher density of 1 m x 0.5 m or 1 m x 0.75 m may be used.

triples.subject: Spacing
triples.source_sentence: For multiplication of stems, rather than production of roots, a closer spacing of 0.5 m x 0.5 m can be used.

triples.subject: Spacing
triples.source_sentence: The recommended optimal planting density in a cassava-maize intercrop is 10,000 cassava plants (1 m x 1 m spacing) and 40,000 - 50,000 maize plants per hectare.

triples.subject: Spacing
triples.source_sentence: Irrespective of the type of legume intercropped with cassava, the plant density of cassava should remain at 10,000 per hectare (Figure 2).

triples.subject: Spacing
triples.source_sentence: For groundnuts, the recommended planting arrangement is to broadcast at 25 plants per square metre.

triples.source_sentence: For some legumes it may be recommended to increase the distance between cassava rows but reduce the distance within the cassava rows so to retain the 10,000 per hectare cassava density yet provide larger space for the legumes.

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: In all cases cassava density is 10,000 per hectare but operations for the intercropped legume are easier and may produce higher yields because more space is allocated to them.

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: After the legume harvest, widely spaced rows could be filled with additional cassava plants.

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: If using ridges or mounds, as a general rule erect growing intercrops (such as maize and soybean) are planted half-way down the side of the ridge or mound; more spreading intercrops (such as groundnuts) should be planted first (before cassava) on top of the ridge or mound.

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: If it is a supporting crop to cassava, it should be planted between the ridges.

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: The timing for planting of the accompanying crops depends on the crops involved. Generally, yams, legumes, melons and maize are planted first before cassava.

triples.subject: land
triples.source_sentence: Select fertile land that is lat or on a gentle slope.

triples.subject: land
triples.source_sentence: For land that was previously under cultivation, slash and till but use herbicides if imperata (spear grass) is present; for short fallow, plough cover crop into the soil; for land under long fallow or forest, cut the vegetation and do selective controlled burning of woody material before tillage.

triples.subject: mechanized_system
triples.source_sentence: Under a mechanized system, plough to 15-30 cm depth, disc harrow to 10 cm depth or ridge, or carry out a combination of these operations.

triples.subject: non_mechanized_system
triples.source_sentence: In non-mechanized system, make mounds or ridges.

triples.source_sentence: Generally space cuttings at 1 m x 1 m (10,000 per hectare), but varieties that grow upright without branching can be grown at 1 m x 0.5 m or 1 m x 0.75 m. If growing for multiplication of stems instead of roots 0.5 m x 0.5 m can be used.

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: If intercropping, maintain 10,000 plants per hectare but distance between cassava rows can be increased e.g. 2 m x 0.5 m.

triples.object: 10 to 16 tonnes fresh roots per hectare
triples.source_sentence: By using chemical fertilizers on their cassava, smallholder farmers can increase their yields from about 10 to 16 tonnes fresh roots per hectare.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: Applying nutrients to the soil enables the maintenance of soil health and improves depleted or poor soils.

triples.source_sentence: ASHC works with initiatives in sub-Saharan Africa to encourage the uptake of integrated soil fertility management (ISFM) practices. triples.subject: Integrated Soil Fertility Management Cropping Systems Pocket Guide series
triples.object: improving agronomic use efficiency of the applied nutrients and improving crop productivity
triples.source_sentence: ASHC deines ISFM as: A set of soil fertility management practices that necessarily include the use of fertilizer, organic inputs and improved germplasm combined with the knowledge on how to adapt these practices to local conditions, aiming at optimizing agronomic use eficiency of the applied nutrients and improving crop productivity. All inputs need to be managed following sound agronomic and economic principles.

triples.subject: Cassava bacterial blight (CBB)
triples.source_sentence: The disease is caused by a bacterium (Xanthomonas campestris pv. manihotis).

triples.subject: CBB
triples.object: wounds or openings or scratches on leaves and stems
triples.source_sentence: Often the bacterium gains entry into plants through wounds or openings or scratches on leaves and stems.

triples.subject: CBB
triples.source_sentence: Stems of infected plants are sources of the bacterium that causes the disease.

triples.subject: CBB
triples.source_sentence: The spread of the disease is largely through the use of cuttings derived from infected stems in starting new farms.

triples.subject: CBB
triples.source_sentence: Farm tools particularly cutlasses can easily be used to transmit the disease from farm to farm if tools are not cleaned after work in an infected field.

triples.subject: CBB
triples.object: infected plant to a new susceptible plant
triples.source_sentence: The spread of the disease occurs if the bacterial causal organism is transferred from an infected plant to a new susceptible plant.

triples.subject: water soaked spots or lesions
triples.source_sentence: Distinctive symptoms of the disease include the appearance of water soaked spots or lesions on leaves of infected plants. The spots often start along the veins, margins and tips of leaf blades.

triples.subject: creamy or yellowish brown gummy exudates
triples.source_sentence: In some susceptible cultivars, creamy or yellowish brown gummy exudates are discharged on leaves or stems but often distinctively on leaf petioles of infected plants.

triples.subject: horizontal orientation of petioles
triples.source_sentence: Petioles of blighted leaves are often horizontally orientated to the main stem axis.

triples.subject: dieback of stems
triples.source_sentence: In advanced stages of the disease, dieback of stems is common.

triples.subject: new shoots developing from dead ends of stems
triples.source_sentence: It is common also to find new shoots developing from dead ends of stems of severely infected plants.

triples.subject: grasshoppers
triples.source_sentence: It is common to find grasshoppers on plants showing symptoms of CBB compared to healthy plants in the same area (Figure 7).

triples.subject: CBB_resistant_varieties
triples.source_sentence: In CBB endemic areas or localities with reported cases of the disease, farmers must consciously search for and plant CBB resistant varieties if economic yields of cassava are to be sustained.

triples.subject: CBB_infected_plants
triples.source_sentence: Farmers cultivating susceptible varieties regularly must inspect their plants and remove those showing symptoms of the disease and destroy them through burning.

triples.subject: storage_roots
triples.source_sentence: It is safe to eat storage roots from CBB infected plants.

triples.subject: burning
triples.source_sentence: Farmers cultivating susceptible varieties regularly must inspect their plants and remove those showing symptoms of the disease and destroy them through burning.

triples.subject: burning
triples.source_sentence: If complete outbreaks on whole farms are observed, it may be necessary to harvest roots immediately and destroy stems and leaves and other plant debris through burning.

triples.subject: infected_plant_debris
triples.source_sentence: If complete outbreaks on whole farms are observed, it may be necessary to harvest roots immediately and destroy stems and leaves and other plant debris through burning.

triples.subject: infected_plant_debris
triples.source_sentence: Infected plant debris may also be ploughed deep into soil.

triples.subject: land
triples.source_sentence: In both situations the land must be allowed to fallow for few years (3 years minimum) before it is planted again to cassava.

triples.subject: cereal
triples.source_sentence: After destruction of infected plant debris as described in the preceding section, cereals, grains or legumes can be planted on the same piece of land.

triples.subject: grains
triples.source_sentence: After destruction of infected plant debris as described in the preceding section, cereals, grains or legumes can be planted on the same piece of land.

triples.subject: legumes

triples.subject: quarantine_measures
triples.source_sentence: In cases of localized outbreaks of CBB it may be necessary for a localized quarantine measure to be implemented that ensures that planting materials from CBB outbreak zones are not moved into other communities.

triples.subject: Quarantine authorities
triples.source_sentence: Quarantine authorities must monitor movement of planting materials across borders and ensure that uncertified planting materials are quarantined to be sure of their safety.

triples.subject: Quarantine authorities
triples.source_sentence: Quarantine authorities must monitor movement of planting materials across borders and ensure that uncertified planting materials are quarantined to be sure of their safety.

triples.subject: Tissue_culture_materials
triples.source_sentence: Tissue culture materials from unreliable laboratories or sources must pass quarantine regulations before they are allowed into cropping systems of countries.

triples.subject: Farmers
triples.source_sentence: Farmers must consciously harvest stems from healthy plants completely free of any of the described symptoms of the disease.

triples.subject: Farmers
triples.source_sentence: It is generally wise to avoid using planting materials from any farm suspected to be under CBB attack even if symptoms of the disease have not been observed on plants.

triples.subject: Grasshoppers
triples.source_sentence: Grasshoppers and other insects that can serve as carriers of the bacterium from farm to farm must be controlled using environmentally friendly measures.

triples.subject: Grasshoppers
triples.source_sentence: Controlling grasshopper movement after the early first rains of the wet season can reduce the spread of CBB.

triples.source_sentence: The disease is caused by a fungus (Collectothricum gloeosporioides) that is also capable of causing diseases on other food crops.

triples.subject: Cassava anthracnose disease (CAD)
triples.source_sentence: Cracks when present serve as entry points for other disease causing organisms.

triples.subject: Cassava anthracnose disease (CAD)
triples.source_sentence: The symptoms of the disease often start and develop rapidly in the wet season.

triples.subject: Cassava anthracnose disease (CAD)
triples.source_sentence: It is estimated that CAD causes yield losses in the neighbourhood of 30% or more in susceptible cultivars.

triples.subject: ministem cuttings
triples.source_sentence: Under the method described above, ministem cuttings are nursed for 4 to 6 weeks in polythene bags or nursery beds filled with garden soil before they are transplanted into the field.

triples.subject: ministem cuttings
triples.source_sentence: Large quantities of soil (over 5 tons on an ovendried basis) are needed to nurse cuttings for planting in 1 hectare, and the soil usually has to be excavated from another site and transported to the nursery.

triples.subject: ministem cuttings
triples.source_sentence: About 50 man-days are required to fill the bags with soil to nurse cuttings for planting in 1 hectare; additional labor is needed to plant one cutting per bag (20 000 or more plants per hectare) and to care for the plants prior to transplanting.

triples.subject: ministem cuttings
triples.source_sentence: The soil used could carry disease-causing organisms such as nematodes, fungi and bacteria.

triples.subject: ministem cuttings
triples.source_sentence: Sterilizing the soil to overcome this problem is expensive and facilities to do this are not easily available.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: If the field is maintained properly, stems can be cut and supplied to farmers or institutions from 6 to 7 months after transplanting.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: They are cut at a height of 20 to 25cm from the ground after it has been ascertained that they are physiologically mature and pest- and disease-free.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: This practice of leaving the stumps standing in the field after harvest is known as 'ratooning'.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: Several shoots sprout from a ratoon left in the field but these are reduced to two or three.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: Another set of stems is cut again about 6 months later.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: At IITA, as many as three ratoons have been taken from rapid multiplication plants.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: Stems must be handled with care throughout the harvesting, loading, transporting and unloading procedures, to avoid too much bruising. If axillary buds are bruised, they may never develop into plants if the nodes are used in rapid multiplication.

triples.subject: Cassava stems
triples.object: special effort by those people who are responsible for making the materials available to farmers
triples.source_sentence: Cassava stems are bulky and do .not store well for a long time. Their transportation and distribution, therefore, deserve special effort by those people who are responsible for making the materials avail- able to farmers.

triples.subject: Cassava stems
triples.source_sentence: As planting materials, it is important for cassava stems to be properly stored. Long-term storage is not possible because stems dehydrate during storage. They are also attacked by insects and diseases,.which results in a lower sprouting percentage.

triples.subject: Tissue_Culture
triples.source_sentence: It may be defined as the culture of single plant cells, a group of cells, tissues or organs in an artificial environment under aseptic conditions. Within such an environment, the cells, tissues and organs multiply and continue to grown in an unorganized way or regenerate into a whole plant. The phrase in vitro, which means 'growing outside the living body, in an artificial environment' is often used in association with tissue culture.

triples.subject: cassava stem cuttings
triples.source_sentence: In general, cuttings taken from the older, more mature parts of the stem give a better yield than those taken from the younger portions.

triples.subject: green stems
triples.source_sentence: Although cuttings from green stems will sprout, they are extremely susceptible to attack by soil-borne pathogens and sucking insects.

triples.subject: immature herbaceous green stems
triples.object: high water content and tend to dehydrate rapidly
triples.source_sentence: Also, the immature herbaceous green stems cannot be stored for a long period because they have a high water content and tend to dehydrate rapidly.

triples.subject: stem cuttings
triples.object: high lignification and small amounts of food reserves
triples.source_sentence: When stem cuttings are taken from plants more than 18 months old, the stem is highly lignified and contains only small amounts of food reserves for the shoots.

triples.subject: stem cuttings
triples.source_sentence: It is recommended that planting material be taken from plants which are between 8 and 18 months old.

triples.subject: thick stems
triples.object: weak shoots and few, small tuberous roots
triples.source_sentence: Although any part of the cassava stem can be used for propagating material in a commercial operation, thin stems which have poor nutrient reserves should not be used. This is because the shoots which develop from such stems tend to be weak and only a few, small tuberous roots are produced.

triples.subject: stem cuttings
triples.object: low percentages of sprouting under field conditions
triples.source_sentence: Cuttings with one to three nodes have low percentages of sprouting under field conditions because they are short and thus have lower food reserves and are more susceptible to pathogen attack and rapid dehydration.

triples.subject: cuttings with few buds
triples.object: loss of viability of all their buds during propagation, transportation and planting
triples.source_sentence: Cuttings with few buds are more likely to lose the viability of all their buds during propagation, transportation and planting.

triples.subject: long cuttings with more than 10 nodes
triples.object: better chance of conserving their viability
triples.source_sentence: Long cuttings with more than 10 nodes theoretically have a better chance of conserving their viability because of the greater number of buds.

triples.subject: long cuttings
triples.source_sentence: Long cuttings have been reported to give higher yields than short ones, presumably because the former had more buried nodes than the latter and thus produced more stems and leaves, which resulted in higher yields.

triples.subject: long cuttings
triples.source_sentence: However, when long cuttings are used, much more propagating material per unit of surface area is required.

triples.subject: cuttings
triples.source_sentence: The recommendation is that cuttings should have five to seven nodes and a minimum length of 20cm.

triples.subject: cuttings
triples.source_sentence: Propagation material should be selected from disease-free plants.

triples.subject: cassava_stands
triples.source_sentence: Generally, cassava stands from which planting material is to be obtained should be cut as close to planting time as possible.

triples.subject: cuttings
triples.source_sentence: It is very important to avoid rough handling when cutting and transporting the selected stems or branches.

triples.subject: cuttings
triples.source_sentence: The epidermis and buds of cuttings may be bruised or damaged by friction and machete wounds during preparation, transportation, storage and planting; each wound is a potential site of entry for micro-organisms that cause rot during storage or after planting.

triples.subject: cuttings

triples.source_sentence: The grated cassava mash is fermented and dehydrated. This is done by putting it in sacks. It also enhances the potential for cassava growers in Africa to develop non-traditional cassava products (such as cassava starch, an important raw material in the food, textile, paper and other industries; cassava flour, for use in various bakery preparations, alone or as composite flour; and cassava chips and pellets, which are incorporated in animal feed rations by EEC countries because of the low price and high energy content of cassava compared with cereals).

triples.subject: improved method
triples.source_sentence: The objectives of improved cassava processing are: to reduce the drudgery and labor intensiveness of traditional cassava processing methods, and thus increase productivity to produce an end product of better and more uniform quality to ensure the reduction or total elimination of undesirable toxic constituents in cassava so that it is suitable for human con- sumption

triples.subject: Freshly uprooted cassava
triples.source_sentence:
Freshly uprooted cassava is preferred because it gives a 
 better-quality product. However, tubers which are from 1 to 3 
 days old may be used if there is no obvious spoilage.

triples.subject: Sliced chips
triples.source_sentence:
In the first drying stage, the sliced chips are dried in the sun for 
 about 3 days to a moisture content 07 14%. Drying is done on 
 trays made of wood or other plant material. During the rainy 
 season, protected solar driers are recommended.

triples.source_sentence:
The chips are soaked in water for 8 hours in tanks; a drain 
 leads from the tank. The ratio of water to chips is 1 gallon of 
 water to 1 pound of chips.

triples.source_sentence:

 dried to a rnoisutre content of 6 to 8%. Ovens with a capacity 
 todry 200kg of chips per batch and handle about four batches 
 a day may be used.

triples.subject: Cassava starch
triples.source_sentence: Cassava starch is an important industrial raw material which is used in the manufacture of a number of products, including food, adhesives, thickening agents and pharmaceuticals.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: Tubers contain 20% starch by weight, but as a result of losses during processing this is reduced to 10%. Thus, 1 ton of cassava produces 100kg of cassava starch.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: When selecting tubers for starch production, age and tuber quality are the critical factors.

triples.subject: stream water
triples.source_sentence: The peeled tubers are washed in cemented tanks. As water quality is not critical at this stage, stream water can be used.

triples.subject: rasaiutt
triples.source_sentence: The percentage of starch set free is called 'rasping effect'. Its value after one rasping varies between 70 and 90%.

triples.subject: woven basket
triples.source_sentence: For a 200kg/day starch production, the cheapest way to wash out the starch is to use a woven basket with a piece of clean calico cloth tied around the outside. This forms a double sieve. The grated pulp is put into the basket and handwashed with water until no more milky starch comes out. The remaining pulp is discarded; The milky starch solution is collected into plastic drums (30-gallon drums are a convenient size for starch removal) and left to settle overnight.

triples.subject: Completely Randomized Design
triples.source_sentence: Unless the experimental site is absolutely uniform (which is never the case in practice), some form of random allocation of varieties or treatments to individual plots is necessary in order to avoid any systematic treatment bias.

triples.subject: Completely Randomized Design
triples.source_sentence: The form of the analysis of this design is to apportion the total 'variation' between the yields of the various plots into that part which can be attributed to treatment effects and a remaining residual part which gives an estimate of the 'variation due to sampling error'.

triples.subject: Completely Randomized Design
triples.source_sentence: In practice, the Completely Randomized Design is used only when the experimental site is extremely uniform (for example, in a laboratory or greenhouse).

triples.subject: Randomized Complete Block Design
triples.source_sentence: In Randomized Complete Block Design, the treatments are grouped into blocks (or replicates) containing 1 plot of each treatment arranged at random.

triples.subject: Randomized Complete Block Design
triples.source_sentence: Randomized Complete Block Design usually offers a considerable advantage over the Completely Randomized Design.

triples.subject: Completely Randomized Design
triples.source_sentence: Randomized Complete Block Design usually offers a considerable advantage over the Completely Randomized Design.

triples.subject: Residual_Variance
triples.source_sentence: Whereas In the Completely Randomized Design these effects remain part of the residual variation, in the Randomized Block Design the residual variation is decreased by the removal of these block effects.

triples.subject: Standard_Error(SE)
triples.source_sentence: the square root of this measure is termed the 'Standard Error (SE) of a single plot', which is an estimate of the standard deviation (SD) of individuals.

triples.subject: F_test
triples.source_sentence: a prior step in testing significance is normally an overall test of all treatments by comparing the treatment variance with the error variance; this is termed the F test.

triples.subject: t-test
triples.source_sentence: Thus SEs of treatment means and SEs of differences between treatment means can be calculated, allowing a t-test to be carried out between a given pair of treatments.

triples.subject: Agronomic trials
triples.source_sentence: Research experiments aimed at investigating field-crop production andlor soil management practices.

triples.subject: Apical dominance
triples.source_sentence: The condition whereby the shoot apex regulates the growth and development of the lateral buds and branches. Auxin, a growth hormone, has been indicated as involved in the process.

triples.subject: Apomixis
triples.source_sentence: Reproduction involving specialized generative tissues but not dependent on fertilization (for example, seed development in the ovary of sexually reproducing plants where the embryo is formed without union of sperm and eggj.

triples.subject: Arthropods
triples.source_sentence: Animals with jointed legs, including Crustacea, Myriopoda, lnsecta and Arachnoidea.

triples.subject: Axillary bud
triples.source_sentence: A bud formed in the axil of a leaf.

triples.subject: Bacteria
triples.source_sentence: Unicellular micro-organisms belonging to the Kingdom Protista , producing no chlorophyll. They reproduce by binary fission and are related to the fungi. Most are saprophytic, some are autotrophic, and some are parasitic to plants and animals.

triples.subject: Biotics
triples.source_sentence: Pertaining to life.

triples.subject: Breeder seed
triples.source_sentence: Purest form of planting material (for example, cassava stem cuttings) of an improved variety produced by the breeder or hislher agents. The quantity of such material is usually small, and further multiplication at experimental or other sites controlled by a station is necessary to increase the quantity. The resulting material from this multiplication is referred to as foundation seed.

triples.subject: Cambium
triples.source_sentence: A layer, usually 1 or 2 cells thick, of persistently meristematic tissue that divides to give rise to secondary tissues, resulting in growth in diameter.

triples.subject: Cerwspora
triples.source_sentence: A common parasitic fungus in the subdivision Senteromycotina. It causes leaf spots on different monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous plants. The genus Cercospora is responsible for three leaf spot diseases of cassava.

triples.subject: Chlorotic
triples.source_sentence: The loss of chlorophyll content by a tissue. Usually, tissue turns yellow or pale or even white. The condition is termed chlorosis and may be brought about by disease, genetic factors, lack of light and deficiency in magnesium or iron.

triples.subject: Linamarin
triples.source_sentence: Substance called Linamarin found in cassava. Linamarin hydrolyzes in the presence of enzymes (linamarase), giving rise to hydrocyanic acid (HCN).

triples.subject: Hydrocyanic acid (HCN)
triples.source_sentence: A very toxic compound found in many plants, including cassava. In cassava, HCN is concentrated mainly in the peel of the tuber and in the leaves.

triples.subject: Xanthomonas campestris pv cassava
triples.source_sentence: A portion of plant tissue devoid of chlorophyll (chlorotic) which surrounds some leaf spots (for example, the chlorotic halo surrounding the bacterial angular leaf spot of cassava caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv cassava@).

triples.subject: Xanthomonas campestris pv manihotis
triples.source_sentence: Host-specific pathogens cannot attack any plants other than their host (for example, Xanthomonas campestris pv manihotis has not been shown to attack any plant apart from cassava, hence it is host-specific).

triples.subject: Xanthomonas campestris pv manihotis
triples.source_sentence: Host-specific pathogens cannot attack any plants other than their host (for example, Xanthomonas campestris pv manihotis has not been shown to attack any plant apart from cassava, hence it is host-specific).

triples.subject: chlorotic halo
triples.source_sentence: A portion of plant tissue devoid of chlorophyll (chlorotic) which surrounds some leaf spots (for example, the chlorotic halo surrounding the bacterial angular leaf spot of cassava caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv cassava@).

triples.subject: Leaf picrate method
triples.source_sentence: A rapid means of testing the amount of HCN released by discs cut from cassava leaves where the quantity of HCN corresponds to the intensity of color (dark red for high HCN) developed when a filter paper soaked in sodium picrate is suspended in a vial containing the leaf disc and a few drops of toluene.

triples.subject: Lesion
triples.source_sentence: A wound; a well-marked but limited diseased area.

triples.subject: Meristem culture
triples.object: the apical dome.tissue distal to the youngest leaf primordia
triples.source_sentence: Apical meristem culture; cultivation of the apical dome.tissue distal to the youngest leaf primordia in prepared nutrient media.

triples.subject: Mycelium
triples.source_sentence: A collection of fungal filaments (hyphae).

triples.subject: Necrosis
triples.object: the death of part of or the whole of a plant
triples.source_sentence: The death of part of or the whole of a plant.

triples.subject: Outcross
triples.object: a progeny resulting from interbreeding involving relatively unrelated individuals
triples.source_sentence: A progeny resulting from interbreeding involving relatively unrelated individuals.

triples.subject: Parthenogenetic
triples.object: plants developed from seed or ovum without fertilization by pollen
triples.source_sentence: Plants developed from seed or ovum without fertilization by pollen.

triples.subject: Perennial
triples.object: a plant that lives an indefinite number of years (perennis: lasting for the whole year)
triples.source_sentence: A plant that lives an indefinite number of years (perennis: lasting for the whole year)

triples.subject: Plantlet
triples.object: a small rooted shoot or germinated embryo
triples.source_sentence: A small rooted shoot or germinated embryo.

triples.subject: Polyploid
triples.object: having or being a chromosome number that is a multiple greater than 2 of the genetic number
triples.source_sentence: Having or being a chromosome number that is a multiple greater than 2 of the genetic number.

triples.subject: propagation
triples.object: methods of raising or establishing crop plants
triples.source_sentence: Methods of raising or establishing crop plants.

triples.subject: Pubescence
triples.object: quality or state of being covered with soft short hairs
triples.source_sentence: Quality or state of being covered with soft short hairs (pubescent: covered with soft hair, as is the case with young leaves and shoots of some cassava varieties.

triples.subject: Recombination
triples.object: the formation through the processes of crossing-over and independent assortment of new combinations of genes in progeny that did not occur in the parents
triples.source_sentence: The formation through the processes of crossing-over and independent assortment of new combinations of genes in progeny that did not occur in the parents.

triples.subject: Recurrent selection
triples.object: a plant-breeding practice whereby progenies from intermating of a group of parents selected for their breeding values are tested for good performance. Selected plants are constituted as parents of the next generation through intermating
triples.source_sentence: A plant-breeding practice whereby progenies from intermating of a group of parents selected for their breeding values are tested for good performance. Selected plants are constituted as parents of the next generation through intermating.

triples.subject: Replication
triples.source_sentence: Systematic or random repetition of experimental units like agricultural test rows or plots to reduce error.

triples.subject: Rogueing
triples.source_sentence: The removal of unwanted varieties or plants of undesired characteristics to prevent them from mixing with or contaminating the desired variety.

triples.subject: Secondaty thickening
triples.source_sentence: Formation of additional, secondary vascular tissue by activity of cambium, with accompanying increase in diameter of stems and roots of plants; providing additional conducting and supporting tissue for the growing plant.

triples.subject: Species
triples.source_sentence: A group of interbreeding individuals not interbreeding with another such group; a systematic unit which includes geographic races and varieties and is included in a genus.

triples.subject: Stem puncture method
triples.source_sentence: Procedure whereby cassava stems are punctured with a needle for inoculation purposes. Usually, plant pathogens are inoculated into such punctures.

triples.subject: Subculture
triples.source_sentence: Subdivision of a culture for transfer to fresh medium.

triples.subject: Supra-optimal temperature
triples.source_sentence: The temperature most ideal for a biological process such as disease development or the growth of a fungus or bacterium.

triples.subject: Systemic
triples.source_sentence: Generally distributed throughout the system (that is, the plant system).

triples.subject: Tetranychids
triples.source_sentence: Having to do with mites.

triples.subject: Tuber
triples.source_sentence: A thickened, fleshy underground root or stem.

triples.subject: Variation
triples.source_sentence: The divergence in the structural or physiological characters of an organism or biotype from those typical or usual to its group; the extent or range of such divergence.

triples.subject: Vascular necrosis
triples.source_sentence: Death of the plant vascular system.

triples.subject: Vector
triples.source_sentence: A carrier of pathogenic organisms; any agent transferring a parasite to a host.

triples.subject: Viral
triples.source_sentence: Consisting of or due to a virus.

triples.subject: Virus
triples.source_sentence: One of the nucleoprotein-like entities a u ~ ~ LO pass through bacteria-retaining filters, having many characteristics of living organisms and recognized by its toxic or pathogenic effects in plants and animals, including man.

triples.subject: Volunteer seedlings
triples.source_sentence: Seedlings resulting from seeds other than those intentionally sown (for example, through germination of seeds from an earlier planting).

triples.subject: Xanthomonas
triples.source_sentence: One of the five bacteria genera pathogenic to plants. The genus is usually characterized by rod shape with a single polar flagellum and yellow colonies (with a few exceptions), and causes angular necrotic leaf spots, gum exudation, wilt, and die-back of young shoots (for example, Xanthomonas campestris or -manihotis).

triples.subject: Soil_sample
triples.source_sentence: 1. Dig the soil to about 10cm deep and take a soil sample at that depth. Wet a handful of the earth with water and rub it on the palms. If it forms a continuous thread, then it can retain water and is good for fish pond construction (Fig. 5).

triples.subject: Water Source and Supply
triples.source_sentence: Water is the medium for fish growth and it is the major limiting factor in fish culture. Water sources must be free from pollutants. These are substances either in effluent or solid forms that are toxic to fish.

triples.subject: Nature of the Soil/Land Availability
triples.source_sentence: Land is a major factor of production. Fish ponds are built on land either by excavating the soil or by building embankment structures. A prospective fish farmer should therefore ensure that the land to be used is legally acquired, this is important since a fish pond structure can be maintained for as long as ten to fifteen years in production cycles.

triples.subject: Nature of the Soil/Land Availability
triples.source_sentence: Soil at the site to be chosen must be tested for its capacity to retain water. A good soil for fish culture must be able to hold water.

triples.subject: Pervious Soil
triples.source_sentence: Pervious soil have very little water retaining capacity, and are very sandy or of mixed gravel and sand. Such soils should be avoided.

triples.subject: soil_percolation_rate
triples.source_sentence: A bucket full of water can also be gradually poured into the dugged hole. If the percolation rate (speed of disappearance of the water into the soil) is fast (i.e. within 1 minute) the site is not likely to retain water for fish pond.

triples.source_sentence: there is the risk of the stumps tearing nets at harvesting. Therefore as much as possible lands that are thickly vegetated should be avoided or the sites should be properly cleared.

triples.subject: Savannah_belt
triples.source_sentence: Sites in the Savannah belt are cheaper to clear since there are fewer trees and roots to be removed.

triples.subject: project_site
triples.source_sentence: The site must be within reach for ease of management and supervision. Such a site will also facilitate marketing of products especially for large-scale operators.

triples.subject: project_site
triples.source_sentence: The project site must be kept to wade off thieves from harvesting the fish. Site must also be protected from natural enemies of fish like water snakes, water birds, frogs, etc. The pond water should be free from domestic interference and access to cattle. Hoofs of cattle can damage pond wall.

triples.subject: project_site
triples.source_sentence: Both skilled manpower and casual labourers must be available to manage the pond especially in large fish farms. Farmers should know the nearest location of research and extension staff in fisheries and other service providers. This formation can be obtained from the Ministry of Agriculture, Research Institutes or Fish Farmers Associations that are nearby.

triples.subject: project_site
triples.source_sentence: Fish farming inputs include fish seeds (fingerlings), supplementary feeds, fertilizers/manures, and other fish pond accessories. Prospective farmers should obtain information from the Ministry of Agriculture on how to source these inputs from the locality.

triples.subject: Fish species
triples.source_sentence: Fish species that are likely to attract high market prices should be grown in the pond.

triples.subject: Pond shape
triples.source_sentence: The shape and size of the pond should fit in with the topography of the land.

triples.subject: Pond size
triples.source_sentence: The assurance of a regular and good source of water supply and land that can retain water for fish culture is the impetus the farmer needs in planning how large the pond should be and how many of a particular unit or units should be constructed.

triples.subject: Pond bottom slope
triples.source_sentence: The bottom of the pond should be sloping to the point close to the embankment where drainage facilities (outlets) will be installed. The slope should be 1:2.

triples.subject: Water inlet location
triples.source_sentence: The water inlet(s) to the pond should be placed preferably at the shallowest end.

triples.subject: Pond drainage
triples.source_sentence: If more than one pond is constructed it is better to have independent water supply (inlets) to each pond and also separate outlets.

triples.subject: Parallel ponds
triples.source_sentence: If more than one pond is constructed it is better to have independent water supply (inlets) to each pond and also separate outlets. By this it would be possible to drain the water from each pond without the water having to flow through a second pond. Such ponds are called parallel ponds (Fig. 3).

triples.subject: Pond Size
triples.source_sentence: For family owned ponds it is advisable to limits the size of each pond to a maximum of 0.2 ha if the water supply is adequate and land is available.

triples.subject: Pond Size
triples.source_sentence: ponds of 0.01ha units are suitable for homestead fish culture.

triples.subject: Pond Size
triples.source_sentence: Earthen ponds meant for commercial purposes should not have total area less than 0.25ha.

triples.subject: RULE 1
triples.object: Always feed fish at the same time and place.
triples.source_sentence: RULE 1: Always feed fish at the same time and place. Fish become trained and learn when and where they are fed. Two feedings per day are normal. Half of the daily amount is given about mid-morning and half in the early afternoon.

triples.subject: RULE 2
triples.source_sentence: RULE 2: Never overfeed the fish

triples.subject: RULE 2
triples.object: Give only as much feed as the fish will consume in 20 minutes or less.
triples.source_sentence: RULE 2: Never overfeed the fish. Give only as much feed as the fish will consume in 20 minutes or less. Uneaten feed will pollute the water and increase the cost of raising your fish. When accumulated uneaten feed decomposes water may become low in dissolved oxygen. In such ponds, fish will usually be seen at the pond surface in the predawn hours gulping air. They will die if the oxygen concentration in the water becomes too low. Steps must be taken to exchange or aerate the pond water. Feeding should be temporarily suspended when dissolved oxygen is low to improve water quality.

triples.subject: RULE 2
triples.object: An obvious inability of the fish to consume all of the feed offered within a 20-minute period.
triples.source_sentence: 1. An obvious inability of the fish to consume all of the feed offered within a 20-minute period. A farmer can walk into the feeding area of his pond 20 minutes after feeding and feel the pond bottom. If a large amount of feed is stirred up, too much feed is being offered. Feed may also be placed on trays or plat forms, which are lowered into the water. These platforms can then be pulled up after feeding to determine the quantity of feed consumed.

triples.subject: RULE 2

triples.subject: RULE 2

triples.subject: Fish Predators
triples.object: Water snakes, turtles, frogs, water birds (king fisher and water duck, etc), crocodiles, crabs, Wild carnivorous fish
triples.source_sentence: Predators are natural enemies of fish. Common fish predators that should be prevented from causing fish losses in ponds include water snakes, turtles, frogs, water birds (king fisher and water duck, etc), crocodiles, crabs, etc. Wild carnivorous fish intruding into ponds are also predators and as such should be prevented.

triples.subject: Regular clearing of pond site
triples.source_sentence: (1) Ensure regular clearing of pond site. Predators hide in bushes.

triples.subject: Fencing the pond site and screening the top, especially concrete tanks
triples.source_sentence: (2) As much as possible, the farmer should fence the pond site and screen the top, especially concrte tanks.

triples.subject: Protecting the pond from flood water
triples.object: Aquatic predators getting into the pond
triples.source_sentence: (3) Most aquatic predators get into the pond through flood water measures should be taken to protect the pond from flood water.

triples.subject: Hunting predators using traps or point blank killing
triples.source_sentence: (4) Hunt the predators, using traps or point blank killing.

triples.subject: Test Cropping

triples.subject: Test Cropping
triples.source_sentence: After examination, test cropped fish should be returned to the pond water.

triples.subject: Test Cropping
triples.source_sentence: A scoop net is suitable for test cropping (Figure. 16).

triples.subject: Partial Harvesting
triples.source_sentence: When different age group of the same fish species or different species combination are reared together in pond, the fish are bound to mature to table sizes at different times.

triples.subject: Partial Harvesting
triples.source_sentence: Partial harvest of pond should be done with appropriate mesh size.

triples.subject: Partial Harvesting
triples.source_sentence: Matured fish can be selected for market sale or family consumption while undersized ones should be returned to the pond.

triples.subject: Partial Harvesting
triples.source_sentence: Periodical harvesting of pond fish enables a farmer to generate revenue periodically.

triples.subject: Partial Harvesting
triples.source_sentence: Draw net in most suitable for harvesting pond fish. (Figure. 17).

triples.subject: Total Harvest

triples.subject: Total Harvest
triples.source_sentence: Total pond harvest from management point of view can be carried out at the end of a production cycle or in cases of emergency like diseases out break.

triples.subject: Total Harvest
triples.source_sentence: A Draw Net or Drag Net is most suitable for total cropping of pond fish.

triples.subject: Total Harvest
triples.source_sentence: Nets should be cleaned and spread in the sun to dry after harvesting operation. This is to preserve and prolong their operational life span.

triples.subject: dry days
triples.source_sentence: On dry days during the snail growing season, water the ground daily. Always water in the evening at sunset. Ensure that the soil is moist and not wet. triples.subject: Sensitivity
triples.source_sentence: z Sensitivity is the number of true cases a system correctly identi es out of the total number of truly diseased subjects studied. The higher the sensitivity of the system, the more truly diseased cases are identi ed (hence a lower number of false negative cases).

triples.subject: Specificity
triples.source_sentence: z Speci city is the number of non-diseased animals a system correctly identi es out of the total number of truly non-diseased subjects examined. The higher the speci city of a system, the more truly non-diseased animals identi ed (hence a lower number of false positive cases).

triples.subject: Timely
triples.source_sentence: The system should be able to detect, investigate, provide feedback and allow for action on a suspect disease event within a timeframe relative to the infectious cycle of the disease.

triples.subject: Representative
triples.source_sentence: The system should re ect the true occurrence and distribution of the event in all communities, production systems and social strata.

triples.subject: Flexible
triples.source_sentence: The system should be able to detect and accommodate emerging diseases.

triples.subject: Simple
triples.source_sentence: If the procedures are too dif cult farmers and surveillance staff will probably not be motivated to report, act and control suspect disease events.

triples.subject: Ownership
triples.source_sentence: Stakeholders should feel a sense of ownership based on their participation in the design of the system and the relevance of the output to their needs.

triples.subject: Passive_surveillance
triples.source_sentence: Passive surveillance, which captures information from existing data sources such as disease reports from livestock keepers, community-based animal health workers, and public and private veterinarians; diagnostic laboratory submissions and abattoir reports. It is a continuous process involving routine collection of information on a wide range of diseases, e.g. in form of monthly reports from veterinary officers to the national disease information system.

triples.subject: Active_surveillance
triples.source_sentence: Active surveillance, which is a speci c exercise or set of exercises to search for a speci c disease or infection in a population or provide evidence of absence of a disease or infection. Methods of active surveillance include the search for clinical disease and/or collection of samples for laboratory analysis. Surveillance may be randomized (e.g. serological surveys) or risk-based depending on its objective.

triples.subject: Participatory_Disease_Surveillance
triples.source_sentence: Participatory Disease Surveillance (PDS) is the application of PE to disease surveillance. PDS is a method of disease surveillance where PA approaches and methods are used to combine local veterinary knowledge with conventional methods to establish the presence or absence of a speci c disease in a particular area.

triples.source_sentence: This method can be used to better understand the local characterization of livestock diseases and the meanings of local names for diseases.

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: It is essentially a series of proportional piling exercises where a list of items, such as diseases, is scored against a number of indicators, such as clinical signs, sources of infection, etc. to create a matrix.

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: Method for matrix scoring of disease syndromes and clinical signs

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: 1. Have a list of five to six common diseases or disease syndromes that the participants have mentioned. Use the same disease names as used by the participants.

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: 2. For each disease, obtain the main clinical signs (indicators) that characterize it.

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: 3. Use pictures, objects or cards to represent the diseases and place these across the top of the matrix.

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: 4. Write the first clinical sign (indicator) on a card or use a picture/object to represent it. Place this to one side of the first row of the matrix.

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: 5. Place a pile of 30 counters next to the indicator and ask the participants to use the 30 counters to show how commonly the clinical sign occurs with each disease. Summarize and crosscheck for agreement on how they have scored.

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: 6. Repeat for each clinical sign one by one, gradually building up the matrix.

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: 7. Record the results in a matrix in your notebook.

triples.subject: Matrix scoring
triples.source_sentence: If possible, leave the counters in the different rows until the end of the exercise so that you create a real matrix that shows the patterns of scoring and the participants can get an idea of the different signs related to which disease.

triples.subject: Introducing new birds
triples.source_sentence: Farmers should not mix birds from different sources.

triples.subject: Introducing new birds
triples.source_sentence: If farmers want to introduce new birds to their flock, they should keep the new bird or birds separate from the flock for at least two weeks before they allow it to have contact with the other birds.

triples.subject: Don't mix different species
triples.source_sentence: It is also important that poultry keepers do not mix different types of poultry (e.g. chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys, guinea fowls, pigeons) in the same enclosure or area.

triples.subject: Protecting village and backyard poultry
triples.source_sentence: The interview Protecting village and backyard poultry begins by looking at some of the major routes by which avian flu can be spread to backyard poultry, and then discusses what village poultry keepers can do to protect their birds from the disease.

triples.subject: Protecting commercial poultry farms from infection
triples.source_sentence: Many of the same rules that apply to backyard poultry also apply to commercial farms: using clean sources of food and water, buying new birds from sources that are registered and disease-free, practising an 'all in, all out' system of rearing.

triples.subject: Protecting commercial poultry farms from infection

triples.subject: Protecting commercial poultry farms from infection
triples.source_sentence: Commercial farms should also have tight biosecurity rules.

triples.subject: Protecting commercial poultry farms from infection
triples.source_sentence: controlling who and what enters the farm;

triples.subject: Protecting commercial poultry farms from infection
triples.source_sentence: ensuring that anyone entering the farm is disinfected and their boots or shoes are cleaned with disinfectant;

triples.subject: Protecting commercial poultry farms from infection
triples.source_sentence: keeping poultry houses and cages very clean;

triples.subject: Protecting commercial poultry farms from infection
triples.source_sentence: daily cleaning of all equipment used in the poultry houses, such as feeding scoops, shovels, brooms and feeding trays;

triples.subject: Protecting commercial poultry farms from infection

triples.source_sentence: Moloi In areas affected by the avian flu, what are the advantages of keeping poultry in fenced enclosures?

triples.subject: Celia Abolnik
triples.source_sentence: Abolnik Obviously if your birds are fenced they are separated from birds that are free ranging that might be carrying infectious diseases.

triples.subject: Celia Abolnik
triples.source_sentence: Abolnik In the ideal situation you would want an enclosed structure, but the best thing to do is not to leave open food and water that will attract wild birds into contact with chickens.

triples.subject: Celia Abolnik
triples.source_sentence: Abolnik It must be bird proof, it must be rat proof. The water must be, and the feed must be separated from any contact with birds and rodents from outside.

triples.subject: Celia Abolnik
triples.source_sentence: Abolnik You could use inexpensive materials to build an enclosure that is rat and bird proof.

triples.subject: Celia Abolnik
triples.source_sentence: Abolnik Mud bricks, grass, sheet metal, anything that they have access to.

triples.subject: Celia Abolnik
triples.source_sentence: Abolnik Definitely. A poultry owner should not allow any person just to walk into his poultry enclosure, especially since they may be carrying infected poultry or wild bird faeces on their person, their boots, their shoes, their clothes, their hands, and handling of birds might transmit the disease in that way.

triples.subject: Celia Abolnik
triples.source_sentence: Abolnik There is no special diet that will prevent them getting avian flu, although the importance of good nutrition is vital, because birds that are immuno-suppressed, birds that have a very weak immune system, sometimes due to hunger, or because they are not getting all the nutrients, might be more predisposed to infections, and might suffer and die more if they are infected.

triples.subject: hygiene around the poultry farm
triples.source_sentence: "There are several things which have been implemented. One is the change in the strategy in terms of raising the flocks. Initially we used to have a single flock mixed with the other flocks, may be younger ones, but now, we have to sell one lot before we introduce another one. That's a major change which is obviously affecting our production, since now we are taking much longer to produce one lot of a flock. Again, we have improved the general hygiene around the poultry farm whereby cleanliness is now taken as a priority to make sure that we do not contaminate the flocks."

triples.subject: individuals working in the poultry farm
triples.source_sentence: "There are several things which have been implemented. One is the change in the strategy in terms of raising the flocks. Initially we used to have a single flock mixed with the other flocks, may be younger ones, but now, we have to sell one lot before we introduce another one. That's a major change which is obviously affecting our production, since now we are taking much longer to produce one lot of a flock. Again, we have improved the general hygiene around the poultry farm whereby cleanliness is now taken as a priority to make sure that we do not contaminate the flocks."

triples.subject: workers who are involved in taking care of the flocks
triples.source_sentence: "And another measure which has been implemented is making sure that the individuals working in the poultry farm don't keep any poultry at their homes. Now it is like a serious measure which has to be checked. So it's a general consensus that each worker who is involved in taking care of the flocks should never keep any poultry at his home."

triples.subject: passers-by
triples.source_sentence: "And we are also restricting any passers-by to make sure that they do not contaminate our flock or the farm at large. So it's like a restricted site, much more serious these days than ever before."

triples.subject: farm
triples.source_sentence: There are some measures by which we make sure that the disease never gets into the farm. Some of them are obviously to make sure that our flocks are always kept enclosed in their cages.

triples.subject: farm
triples.source_sentence: And we also keep on checking if at all there are any intruding birds coming in; and those are obviously chased out before they can even have a chance to contaminate our flock.

triples.subject: farm
triples.source_sentence: But if at all we see any suspicious bird, maybe being weak, or whatever, we make sure that it is immediately quarantined and a veterinary officer called to make sure that he assists and check whatever is happening.

triples.subject: farm
triples.source_sentence: That is why we are taking every opportunity to prevent it from coming whilst making sure that if possible, even if it comes, but at least my farm should not be affected by making sure that we implement that advice which has been given by the government.

triples.subject: farm
triples.source_sentence: If it ever comes, then it can definitely be a disaster because apart from losing the market, obviously the economy will be affected since people will definitely be terrified and they would not buy even those chickens which are not affected, and that will definitely be very bad for everyone, loss of jobs, loss of business, and that will be terrible.

triples.subject: droppings and all the surroundings

triples.subject: Wambura
triples.source_sentence: The big risk is from the flock itself. If the flock is clean and it has been confirmed by the authorities that your flock is ok and you proceed with the selling of meat, I think the normal cooking as usual is really safe.

triples.subject: Wambura
triples.source_sentence: So people should not turn away from eating chicken because of the scare of bird flu. As long as the flock has been free from the disease and there is no other confirmation of the disease around, people should take all the precautions, measures of cooking chicken in hygienic conditions. No extra care is really needed, just normal usual cooking until it is really cooked very well, it is no problem at all.

triples.subject: Wambura
triples.source_sentence: I think it is very important to be aware that this disease is normally a bird disease or chicken disease. So we have to be aware of deaths, any suspicions of the disease you have to report it to the authorities, veterinary inspectors and veterinary officers or people who are concerned with welfare of people in all levels from the villages up to the nation, we have to be aware.

triples.subject: Wambura
triples.source_sentence: In those countries where the disease has been reported, normally children are really affected because they play around with dead chickens and they are infected. So we should be really advising children once they see any dead birds or any suspicion of sick birds, they should not really touch them and we should inform the authorities rather than taking for granted that this is a normal death. So any suspicion should be reported and the people should not worry so much about the disease. The only thing you should take precautious measures when you handle chickens in your normal flock, make sure you wash your hands and take precautious measures of whole hygiene.

triples.source_sentence: By making some specific mating, breeders have been able to produce progenies with the cockerel chicks having down colour or rate of growth of the primary wing feathers different from those of the female counterparts at hatching. In this type of cross, which is referred to as 'sex-linked cross', the hens transmit their characters (i.e. down colour pattern or rate of growth of the primary wing feathers) to the cockerel chicks only.

triples.subject: Sexing
triples.source_sentence: Examples of such crosses are: (a) mating Rhode Island Red (RIR) males with Barred Plymouth Rock (BPR) females. The barring characteristic in the (BPR) female is sex-linked and is therefore transferred to the males. At hatching, the cockerel chicks have a white spot on the head and yellow shanks while the pullet chicks are completely black with black shanks.

triples.subject: Sexing

While in the females, the primaries wing feather are shorter than the coverts feather .

triples.subject: Newcastle disease
triples.source_sentence: Newcastle disease in particular, kills as much as 70 - 80% of unvaccinated village hens each year in developing countries.

triples.subject: vaccination campaigns
triples.source_sentence: However vaccination campaigns for village chickens have proved difficult and expensive to organise; poultry owners are very widely spread, making them difficult to reach.

triples.subject: farmers
triples.source_sentence: And apart from a recent vaccine developed in Australia, vaccines for Newcastle disease have needed to be kept cool, requiring an expensive 'cold chain' of refrigeration equipment. Because of the difficulties, few governments are able to provide vaccination campaigns for village chickens.
Feed is the biggest input cost for commercial poultry production (between 60-80% of total costs).

triples.source_sentence: This is a question that will interest many of your listeners; Newcastle disease in particular, kills a high proportion of village chickens each year, but vaccination campaigns have proved difficult to manage. triples.subject: Housing for village hens
triples.object: West, East, Central and Southern Africa
triples.source_sentence: Properly designed and built housing for village chickens protects them from bad weather and predators, and if houses are easy to clean, diseases are less likely to occur. How to build a suitable house for poultry is a difficult subject for radio to tackle, but you could raise the important issues with an invited guest - perhaps an extension officer with expertise in village poultry. Housing for village hens contains some good points about design.

triples.subject: Cross-breeding local chickens
triples.object: West, East, Central and Southern Africa
triples.source_sentence: Selecting the best qualities in local poultry species for cross-breeding can produce significant increases in production and greater tolerance of diseases and environmental conditions. Listeners may be interested to hear from local poultry farmers who have managed to cross-breed their birds successfully. Cross-breeding local chickens could be used to introduce the subject.

triples.subject: Indigenous chickens
triples.source_sentence: The advantages of raising indigenous chickens are: one, they mature early. The second one is that they are cost effective, meaning that there are minimum overheads required or things like electricity, you don't need electricity to raise them. You don't need to go to the market as people are the ones who come and buy them at home. Feeding these chickens is also not expensive as they do not consume much and I always supplement their feeding by giving them crushed grain, sunflower which I grow in my field and sorghum. The other great advantage is that they are resistant to diseases.

triples.subject: artificial lighting
triples.source_sentence: If you have electricity, a chicken house can be lit with ordinary light bulbs.

triples.subject: 40 Watt bulbs
triples.source_sentence: 40 Watt bulbs should be placed 3 m apart and 60 Watt bulbs about 5 m apart.

triples.subject: 60 Watt bulbs
triples.source_sentence: 40 Watt bulbs should be placed 3 m apart and 60 Watt bulbs about 5 m apart.

triples.subject: artificial lighting
triples.source_sentence:
If you use oil lamps, there must be enough of them, and they should be lo-
cated in the centre of the chicken house, and should be screened off with thin slats or wire gauze, even if they are hung up.

triples.subject: chickens
triples.source_sentence: ? If the housing is lit in the cooler hours before sunrise or after sunset, the chickens are able to eat more.

triples.subject: laying hens
triples.source_sentence: ? If the day length is increased by using artificial lighting, laying hens are encouraged to lay more eggs.

triples.subject: chickens
triples.source_sentence: If you are raising laying hens when the days are getting longer, you do not have to provide extra light to stimulate egg production. However, the hens will probably eat more if the housing is lit during the cooler periods of the day.

triples.subject: day length
triples.source_sentence: Just before the laying period starts, lengthen the days by one hour a week until you have 14 hours of light per day.

triples.subject: day length
triples.source_sentence: After production rates have reached a maximum, lengthen the amount of light per day by one hour a week until there are 16 hours of light.

triples.subject: artificial lighting
triples.source_sentence: Once day length has been increased from 12 to 14 hours, you will need to provide artificial light after sunset to maintain the extra day length.

triples.subject: artificial lighting
triples.source_sentence: If you are raising laying hens when the days are getting longer, you do not have to provide extra light to stimulate egg production.

triples.subject: pathogens
triples.source_sentence: The following measures can be applied by both commercial and back-yard poultry farmers.

triples.subject: poultry farm
triples.source_sentence: When starting a poultry farm, keep a distance from other poultry farms or houses. Note the direction the wind normally comes from.

triples.subject: newly bought birds
triples.source_sentence: Beware of bird markets, and always keep newly bought birds apart from your poultry flock for 2 weeks, to be sure they do not carry diseases.

triples.subject: scavenging chickens or ducks
triples.source_sentence: Keep scavenging chickens or ducks apart from your commercial poultry flock, as they can introduce new germs.

triples.subject: visitors
triples.source_sentence: Do not allow any visitors in your chicken houses. Vets are especially dangerous! Make sure that persons entering poultry houses change their footwear.

triples.subject: houses
triples.source_sentence: Make sure your houses, feed storage and water tanks are bird-proof.

triples.subject: used egg trays
triples.source_sentence: Beware of used egg trays. You may not know where they come from.

triples.subject: chickens
triples.source_sentence: Sell chickens, eggs, or old litter outside your farm or at the farm-gate.

triples.subject: different species of birds
triples.source_sentence: Keep different species of birds apart.

triples.subject: birds_of_different_ages
triples.source_sentence: Keep birds of different ages apart, except for hens and their baby chicks.

triples.subject: all-in all-out principle
triples.source_sentence: On larger commercial farms, only keep birds of one age at one time. After each batch, clean and disinfect all the houses. This is the 'all-in all-out principle'.

triples.subject: chicken houses/shelters
triples.source_sentence: Clean drinkers and feeders regularly, making sure that drinkers do not overflow. Put overflowing drinkers on slats or bricks. Provide clean drinking water that is not from a pond, to prevent outbreaks of water-borne diseases like fowl cholera.

triples.subject: Eggs
triples.source_sentence:
Eggs have a high nutritional value. Both the egg-white and yolk con-
tain high quality protein (for both, this is at least 10% of their own 
weight). The egg-yolk has about 33% fat. Eggs also have a lot of vi-
tamin A and D, and some vitamin B.

triples.subject: Eggs
triples.source_sentence:
If you wish to sell eggs, you need a good storage place for them. Only 
store fresh, clean eggs with undamaged shells. The storage place for 
the eggs must be clean and as cool as possible, especially if the eggs 
must be kept for more than a week. A dark space is the most suitable 
for this. If the eggs have been fertilised, it is even more important to 
have a cool storage place. At high temperatures (e.g. above 25 deg C), 
embryo development starts to take place.

will loose part of its value as fertiliser. Keep the manure as dry as pos-
sible. This minimises the loss of minerals and problems with flies.

triples.subject: Moult period
triples.object: After the first production period of 8-10 months
triples.source_sentence: Making use of a moult can be worthwhile if: the purchase price of chickens is high; the egg price is low at the time; the price received for old chickens is also low; better eggshells raise the price received for eggs. The price received for old hens which have stopped laying is usually high in the tropics. Since it is difficult and risky to get all the chickens to moult at the same time, it is probably preferable to keep layers for only one laying period. Chickens in the tropics are said to naturally start moulting after laying for a year. This tends to happen in the season with shorter days. The moult can be stimulated by using extra artificial lighting. It is also possible to trick the chickens into moulting. Limit the first production period of the chickens to only 8-10 months. Then force them to moult by giving them less and poorer quality feed.

triples.subject: African swine fever
triples.source_sentence: Participants said that they had conducted surveillance visits in sub-counties with ASF outbreaks to check if traders closed their business premises (such as slaughter-slabs and pork joints) as obliged, and to get a better understanding of the epidemiological situation.

triples.subject: African swine fever
triples.source_sentence: Overall, farmers were perceived to be the most affected stakeholder; ranked first by three out of four farmer FGDs, two out of four trader FGDs, and both veterinarians FGDs (see Table 4).

triples.subject: African swine fever
triples.source_sentence: Overall, farmers were perceived to be the most affected stakeholder; ranked first by three out of four farmer FGDs, two out of four trader FGDs, and both veterinarians FGDs (see Table 4).

triples.subject: African swine fever
triples.source_sentence: Pork retailers were perceived to be the second most affected stakeholder, being ranked either in first or second position by three out of four farmer FGDs, all four trader FGDs and one of two veterinarian FGDs.

triples.subject: African swine fever
triples.source_sentence: The overall economic impact of quarantine on middlemen was reported as small compared to farmers and pork retailers.

triples.subject: marketable pigs
triples.source_sentence: Impacts mentioned in all FGDs included revenue foregone when marketable pigs could not be sold and the additional cost of feeding marketable pigs during the quarantine period.

triples.subject: pig manure
triples.source_sentence: Additionally, costs associated with constructing temporary pig shelters, feeding of the pigs that would have been managed on free-range if restrictions had not been in place, and the opportunity cost foregone of selling pig manure were mentioned by participants in the four farmers' FGDs.

triples.subject: pork roasting businesses
triples.source_sentence: A participant in FGD2 exemplified this; 'Big, big loss by pork roasters as they never attempted to roast in fear of people detecting smell and smoke from pork joints.'

triples.subject: middlemen
triples.source_sentence: Participants noted that middlemen normally make their business from buying pigs from farmers and selling to butchers, or payments are received from both farmers and butchers for linking transactions.

triples.subject: middlemen
triples.source_sentence: Two traders and one veterinarians' FGDs perceived that middlemen were affected as money that were paid in advance for renting pig holding facilities that remained non-operational during the restriction period could not be recuperated.

triples.subject: tax_collectors
triples.source_sentence: Sellers and buyers of pigs pay market-dues and loading fees in livestock markets.

triples.subject: tax_collectors
triples.source_sentence: The perceived loss of pig slaughter-fees were reported by six FGDs (all four traders' s and all two veterinarians' FGDs) to have affected tax-collectors when slaughter slabs and pork joints were closed.

triples.subject: tax_collectors
triples.source_sentence: The perceived loss of pig slaughter-fees were reported by six FGDs (all four traders' s and all two veterinarians' FGDs) to have affected tax-collectors when slaughter slabs and pork joints were closed.

triples.subject: consumers
triples.source_sentence: All FGDs reported that consumers incurred additional cost for buying substitute for pork that was more expensive (e.g., fish and chicken), and six (four farmers and two traders' FGDs) mentioned costs for hir- ing boda-boda riders to search for pork.

triples.subject: consumers
triples.source_sentence: The price of pork bought illegally was perceived to be higher than the normal pork price by two farmers and two traders FGDs.

triples.subject: veterinarians
triples.source_sentence: Three traders' and both veterinarians' FGDs mentioned that veterinarians lost fees for pork inspection, pork quality assurance at slaughter slabs and movement permit for health certification of pig on transit.

triples.subject: veterinarians
triples.source_sentence: The foregone cost of inspection-fee for ante-mortem examination of live pigs in livestock markets was perceived as affecting veterinarians by two traders and one veterinarian FGDs.

triples.subject: veterinarians
triples.source_sentence: Costs of fuel for collecting pig carcasses from farmers and burning carcasses at district head quarter incurred by veterinarians was mentioned by two farmers and one veterinarian FGDs.

triples.subject: Dr Jerry Abenga
triples.source_sentence: Abenga Because there is no regulation on who sells veterinary drugs, there has been a lot of importation of drugs that have been found to be fake.

triples.subject: Dr Jerry Abenga
triples.source_sentence: Abenga There are several antibiotics, particularly the tetracyclines, that many of them don't have the necessary chemicals to cure diseases.

triples.subject: Dr Jerry Abenga
triples.source_sentence: Abenga And also a lot of drugs meant for the control of ecto-parasites, many of them have no effect on animals.

triples.subject: Dr Jerry Abenga

triples.subject: Animal_health
triples.source_sentence: Just like human beings, we need to be healthy in order to be productive. triples.subject: Proper_feeding
triples.source_sentence: We all know that proper feeding is very very important in maintaining human health. The same thing applies to animals. They need to get a balanced diet: proteins, they need to get vitamins, they need to get energy, they need to get water, mineral salts, they are all very necessary to keep our animals healthy.

triples.subject: Hygiene
triples.source_sentence: Also we need to, just like for human beings, we need to talk of hygiene. We need to have a clean environment where our animals stay.
