triples.subject: Government
triples.source_sentence: And the one issue which maybe I would also like to air out is, the village government is empowered to withdraw all the kits and drugs from the trained community based animal health workers if the performance is dropping down, maybe because of laziness and what have you.

triples.subject: Drug boxes
triples.source_sentence: These drug boxes are in two categories. Some of the drug boxes belong to the Assistant Veterinary Officers. The second category are drug boxes owned by farmer groups themselves.

triples.subject: Farmer technicians
triples.source_sentence: This was the initiative of the Basic Animal Health Services Project whereby we have farmer technicians who we call the 'key men', manning these drug boxes, though some of the boxes still are being manned by the veterinary assistants but those are very few.

triples.subject: Mgomezulu

triples.subject: Mgomezulu
triples.source_sentence: Yes I should say that these drug boxes are very effective, in the sense that we have seen the results. Disease instances have been reduced and we have even seen that livestock numbers, especially the goats as well as the chickens, the numbers are increasing.

triples.subject: Mgomezulu
triples.source_sentence: To ensure that we don't have serious outbreaks of Newcastle Disease we advise farmers to follow the right vaccination schedules. In Malawi we have been using La Sota vaccine mostly and therefore we recommend that they vaccinate the chickens four times in a year. That is vaccinating after each and every three months.

triples.subject: Mgomezulu
triples.source_sentence: But also what I would advise them is to adopt improved husbandry practices. They have to adopt good feeding practices, good housing practices, preventive measures such as de-worming, those are very very important in order to reduce instances of diseases.

triples.subject: Donald Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: Diagnosing what disease an animal has is usually the job of trained veterinary officers. In some cases they will need to send samples from the animal to laboratories for testing. However, these disease diagnosis services are under huge pressure in much of Africa, and are often unable to help farmers living in remote areas.

triples.subject: Donald Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: One of the problems is also literacy because if you get maybe vets who cannot communicate with the local areas there is a language gap. But we have to talk in our local languages; if we get vets who talk in local languages and then have educational tours in the whole district from one area to another.

triples.subject: Donald Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: I've done outreaches myself. We spend nearly the whole day doing lessons about common diseases. And after that I've seen a good improvement from that policy.

triples.subject: Donald Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: What I have done to the communal farmers which I've visited myself, I've had to teach people the common symptoms which animals show. I have taught those guys the common symptoms and then say, as soon as you see these you just call a veterinary extension officer.

triples.subject: Donald Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: And if you had a call, they didn't understand before then you say that I have again to teach them

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: The systems that exist in Zimbabwe at the moment for disease diagnosis they are actually not effective because the veterinary department now is relying mostly on farmers. But farmers sometimes they don't know, they think of other reasons, some even think of witchcraft and so on which is actually wrong.

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: We should have veterinary people in the field where those if they diagnose the disease then we have labs in Harare, for Foot and Mouth actually in South Africa.

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: The problem that we have now is vehicles because some samples we have to rush them, we have to reach within 24 hours in a refrigerated container.

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: And if you are deep in Matabeleland North you don't have vehicles just to travel, to reach Harare takes about 3 days which makes that disease diagnosis actually not effective.

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: So with the teaching that is going on it's actually helping us.

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: Now we have just, there are some diseases which we have grouped on certain symptoms. We should just check that the animal is anaemic, you need to check the gums and then you see they are pale.

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: Then there we just say if you see these diseases, these are tick-borne diseases, if you see this disease then maybe it is a viral disease.

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: Then there we just say if you see these diseases, these are tick-borne diseases, if you see this disease then maybe it is a viral disease.

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: With that then we would treat; the treatment for tick-borne diseases as you know there are 2 or 3 drugs which we use.

triples.subject: Sibanda
triples.source_sentence: And if it is a viral then we avoid movement, letting that animal being stressed and so on, leave that animal at home.

triples.subject: Cold Chain Dosage

triples.subject: Injection Routes

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: Cassava production in Africa occurs within a variety of cropping systems which, on a given parcel of land, could be in the form of: Monocrop - cassava is the only crop on the plot; this is found mainly on large-scale commercial farms.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: Cassava production in Africa occurs within a variety of cropping systems which, on a given parcel of land, could be in the form of: Intercrop - cassava is grown alongside other crops on the same plot at the same time.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: Cassava production in Africa occurs within a variety of cropping systems which, on a given parcel of land, could be in the form of: Crop rotation - this can take two forms:

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: (1) Crop rotation under continuous cropping: This involves continued use of the same parcel of land while alternating the crops grown from one season to the next or from one year to the next.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: (2) Crop rotation nested in fallow: Fallow involves leaving a parcel of land unused for some time to enable soil fertility to build back up before reuse. Some fallows are natural (i.e. the land is left unsown, as commonly practiced in West and Central Africa) while others are managed (i.e. a cover crop is planted on the land to enhance the soil fertility restoration process).

triples.subject: land_types
triples.source_sentence: For less weed-infested land, simply slash and till by hand, oxen or tractor. The minimum option is to slash the vegetation.

triples.subject: land_types

triples.subject: land_types
triples.source_sentence: For planted fallows (e.g. mucuna and pueraria cover crops, which are legumes) simply plough the cover crop biomass into the soil or retain as mulch on the soil surface to increase soil organic matter. Large, woody material should be removed.

triples.subject: land_types

triples.subject: land_types

triples.subject: land_types
triples.source_sentence: With a longer fallow, more woody debris that is hard to incorporate in the soil will be present. Cutting the vegetation and selective controlled burning of woody material should be carried out. Remove tree stumps if tractor tillage is foreseen; stumps can be retained if zero tillage or manual tillage are used. Avoid use of bulldozers as they damage the top soil.

triples.subject: land_types

triples.subject: N-P-K compound fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: If the farmer is using N-P-K compound fertilizer, the total quantity of fertilizer required should be applied in three phases (also called splits):

triples.subject: N-P-K compound fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: One-third of the total quantity required should be applied 4-6 weeks after planting (using quantities calculated from the anticipated or targeted crop yields).

triples.subject: N-P-K compound fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: A second dressing should be applied 10 - 12 weeks after planting.

triples.subject: N-P-K compound fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: The third dressing is recommended 16 - 20 weeks after planting.

triples.subject: N-P-K compound fertilizer
triples.object: 20 cm from the base of the cassava plant
triples.source_sentence: Using a small weeding hoe (10 - 15 cm across), scrape a half-moon shaped furrow 20 cm from the base of the cassava plant (Figure 3).

triples.subject: N-P-K compound fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: Apply the correct measure of fertilizer into the furrow.

triples.subject: N-P-K compound fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: Cover the applied fertilizer with soil.

triples.subject: N-P-K compound fertilizer
triples.object: not applied just before the rain stops
triples.source_sentence: However, this depends on the rainy season: it should not be applied just before the rain stops (Figure 4).

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: For later dressings the use of a hoe may not be appropriate as cassava roots near the surface could be damaged.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: The fertilizer should be applied in a circle or semi-circle around the cassava at 10-20 cm distance.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: If the cassava is planted in wider rows and closer distances within the rows the fertilizer may also be banded along the cassava row at 10-15 cm from the cassava row.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: For example, if the target yield is 16 tonnes per hectare and N-P-K 15-15-15 is being used: 804 kg x 1/3 = 268 kg per hectare N-P-K, which should be applied in each of the three splits.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: If the second rainy season is short and unreliable then the three dressings should be scheduled in closer intervals so as to supply all fertilizer in the first season.

triples.subject: Cassava
triples.source_sentence: If second season rains are reliable the last dressing could be applied once the second season rains have established.

triples.subject: urea

triples.subject: cassava
triples.source_sentence: The standard use efficiency of soils for inorganic fertilizers is about 50% - this means that only half of the nutrients applied are actually utilised by the crop. The farmer should, therefore, apply twice the quantity required to allow for this and to avoid depletion of soil nutrients.

triples.subject: 5.4 kg P
triples.source_sentence: To supply 5.4 kg P requires: 5.4 kg x 100/19.8 = 27.2 kg triple superphosphate (TSP).

triples.subject: 27.2 kg triple superphosphate (TSP)
triples.source_sentence: This amount needs to be doubled to allow for the 50% use efficiency: 27.2 x 2 = 54.4 kg, or about one standard 50 kg bag for each hectare.

triples.subject: 41.4 kg K
triples.source_sentence: To supply 41.4 kg K would require: 41.4 x 100/48 = 86.25 kg potassium chloride (KCl).

triples.subject: 86.25 kg potassium chloride (KCl)
triples.source_sentence: This amount needs to be doubled to allow for the 50% use efficiency: 86.25 kg x 2 = 172.5 kg, or about three and a half standard 50 kg bags per hectare.

triples.subject: 9.5 bags
triples.source_sentence: So, supplying the required nutrients with single nutrient fertilizer requires a total of 9.5 bags per hectare, compared to 16 bags if N-P-K 15:15:15 had been used.

triples.subject: 27.2 kg DAP
triples.source_sentence: The N in 27.2 kg of DAP is 27.2 x 18/100 = 4.9 kg N

triples.subject: 55.1 kg
triples.source_sentence: If supplying 60 kg N (as in the above example), additional N required is 60 - 4.9 = 55.1 kg. This can be supplied by 55.1 x 100/46 = 120 kg of urea.

triples.subject: 54.4 kg of DAP
triples.source_sentence: Assuming 50% use efficiency, about 27.2 x 2 = 54.4 kg of DAP (about one 50 kg bag), 120 x 2 = 240 kg urea (about five 50 kg bags), 86.25 kg x 2 = 172.5 kg of KCl (about three and a half standard 50 kg bags) are needed per hectare.

triples.subject: 172.5 kg of KCl

triples.subject: Input supply
triples.source_sentence: Input supply: This stage is concerned with sourcing of raw materials required for agricultural production, processing, and trade. Marketing/trade inputs: The key inputs for efficient maize marketing are good seed, fertilizers, crop protection products and water. Others include: store/ ware house, Bags, Basins, Wheel barrow, Transport, Market (where sellers and buyers meet) and Consumers.

triples.subject: Production inputs
triples.source_sentence: Production inputs: The key inputs for efficient maize production are good seed, fertilizers, crop protection products, water and land (soil). Processing inputs: The key inputs for efficient maize processing include knives (manual peeling) Big bowls (for manual washing) Mechanical washing machine, grinding machine De-watering (drying) device ( machine or traditional), Filter or sieve, Fryer, Packing Material e.g. bags.

triples.subject: Processing inputs
triples.source_sentence: Processing inputs: The key inputs for efficient maize processing include knives (manual peeling) Big bowls (for manual washing) Mechanical washing machine, grinding machine De-watering (drying) device ( machine or traditional), Filter or sieve, Fryer, Packing Material e.g. bags. Marketing/trade inputs: The key inputs for efficient maize marketing are good seed, fertilizers, crop protection products and water. Others include: store/ ware house, Bags, Basins, Wheel barrow, Transport, Market (where sellers and buyers meet) and Consumers.

triples.subject: Farm Production
triples.source_sentence: Farm Production: This is carried out by farmers with different farm sizes. Farms may range from less than one hectare to thousands of ha) using different types of technology (from hand hoe to large tractors), applying different levels of inputs and with significantly different yield level. This stage is concerned with primary agriculture production and ends with the sale of a raw commodity at the farm gate. These transactions may occur literally at the farm gate or at some other point where the farmer hands over ownership of the product to the next value chain participant. For maize, most of the initial processing operations such as the shelling or bagging of dry grain may take place at the farm level. Maize producers' has different primary objectives either for primary consumption or for commercial sale.

triples.subject: Climate
triples.source_sentence: Maize is grown over a wide range of climatic conditions because of its many divergent types. Sellers of all soil fertility improvement and weather apparatus constitute stakeholders related to soils and climate. Temperature requirement: Maize crop requires warm climate throughout the period of its active life. It does not tolerate low temperature below 13oC which may occur during the dry harmatan period, in which germination is low.

triples.subject: Paddy_cleaner
triples.source_sentence: The paddy cleaner consists of screening and aspiration sections. An oscillating movement applied to the sloping screen by vibratory motors causes paddy to move downward across the screen surface. Paddy cleaners provide screening and aspiration operations in perforated screen (upper screen) removes objects that are appreciably wider than rice (i.e., seed in pods, corn, beans, or other), whereas a round perforated screen (lower screen) removes objects that are significantly shorter than rice. The aspiration section separates light materials from the paddy, allowing the cleaned paddy to drop through to a bottom outlet. The aspiration section removes objects that are significantly lighter than rice (i.e., dust, husks, and such).

triples.subject: Onions
triples.source_sentence: The onions must not have suffered any mutilation during growth or at any time of pulling, removal of the stem, packaging, handling, or any other operation.

triples.subject: Onions
triples.source_sentence: The onions must not be rotten or seriously affected by disease or parasites.

triples.subject: Onions
triples.source_sentence: The bulbs must be free from any impurity, which may materially alter the appearance or quality.

triples.subject: Onions
triples.source_sentence: The onion is regarded as frost-bitten when more than two of the outer layers of the flesh are affected and the flesh has a waxy appearance. A waxy appearance of the outer layers of the flesh can also be caused by mechanical handling. This slight defect does not affect the edibility of the onions. This waxy appearance of the outer layers disappears in a few days after ventilation.

triples.subject: Onions
triples.source_sentence: At the beginning of the season, onions are frequently pulled before fully developed. Although they cannot be stored, they must be covered by a dry skin, which may be sufficiently dry for no moisture to be pressed out by the fingers, in order that any subsequent heating may be avoided. The onions must be pulled when ripe enough to meet current market standards, i.e. such that they remain sufficiently firm and do not become soft or spongy.

triples.subject: Onions
triples.source_sentence: At the time of shipment onions must show no signs of excessive moisture due to unnatural causes (such as prolonged exposure to rain) likely to impair their capacity for travel or keeping qualities. The condensation observed immediately after cold storage is not regarded as 'abnormal'.

triples.subject: Onions
triples.source_sentence: This refers especially to produce that has been in poorly kept or unsuitable cold storage facilities and which may have absorbed the odour given off by other produce on the premises.

triples.subject: Stems
triples.source_sentence: The stems must be twisted or clean-cut and must not be more that 4 cm long (except for stringed onions)

triples.subject: Spring onions
triples.source_sentence: Spring onions mature for harvesting after 35-45 days from sowing.

triples.subject: Bulb onions
triples.source_sentence: Bulbs generally mature within 100-140 days from sowing, depending on the cultivar and the weather.

triples.subject: Bulbs
triples.source_sentence: As a practical guide, farmers should conduct sample counts on the number of bulbs, which have fallen over in a field; and when the percentage of bulbs, which have fallen over, reaches about 70-80% then the entire crop should be harvested.

triples.subject: Bulbs
triples.source_sentence: Harvesting could commence earlier when 50-80% of the tops have gone over, before it is possible to see split skins exposing onion flesh

triples.subject: Windrowing
triples.source_sentence: In traditional small-scale operations, onion drying is carried out in the field in a process commonly called 'windrowing'.

triples.subject: Field Neck Curing
triples.source_sentence: Bulbs harvested for storage require in total 14-20 days of ripening or drying before being stored.

triples.subject: Trays
triples.source_sentence: Harvested onions may also be placed in trays, which are then stacked at the side of the field to dry.

triples.subject: Sheds
triples.source_sentence: In some tropical regions, the bulbs are tied together in groups by plaiting the tops, which are then hung over poles in sheds to dry naturally.

triples.subject: Purpose-built drier
triples.source_sentence: Harvested bulbs can also be taken straight from the field and dried artificially either in a store, shed, barns, or in a purpose-built drier.

triples.subject: Wire mesh
triples.source_sentence: Placing onions on wire mesh in well ventilated conditions and using air at about 30 deg C, 60-75% rh and 150 m .h-1.m-3 is generally recommended for mechanical drying.

triples.subject: string of onions
triples.source_sentence: This is suitable for transporting small quantity of crop, and during storage, the bunches are hung from the roof or from special racks.

triples.subject: shelves
triples.source_sentence: Shelves for onion handling and storage are made from either wooden slats or metal mesh on a wooden or metal frame, and are usually fixed in position with the bulbs loaded and unloaded in the store.

triples.subject: loose bulk
triples.source_sentence: Loose bulk handling of onion is most suitable for large-scale operations where forced ventilation can be provided during long-term storage.

triples.subject: Vidalia Sweets
triples.source_sentence: Soft cultivars (which are also generally sweet) 'Vidalia Sweets' should not be stored in loose bulk because of their high susceptibility to compression and impact damage.

The principal rigid containers are trays (10-15 kg of onions each), boxes (up to 25 kg), and bulk bins (up to 1000 kg). triples.subject: Fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: Fertilizer markets in Africa underwent liberalization to varying degrees beginning in the late 1980s/early 1990s but in many countries there is still government involvement in fertilizer importation and/or distribution to varying degrees.

triples.subject: Fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: The majority of fertilizer consumed in Africa is in granular form. Therefore, either it is imported bagged or it is imported in bulk and bagged at the port at a flat cost per bag using equipment owned by the Port Authority and/or private bagging companies.

triples.subject: Fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: Importation of fertilizer is location-specific, while in most countries its consumption is highly dispersed and located at a distance from the port. Therefore, a reliable and efficient transportation system is required to move fertilizer to farmers in Africa.

triples.subject: Fertilizer
triples.source_sentence: The road network in Africa, particularly in rural areas, is sparse and those that do exist are poorly maintained. This results in high maintenance costs for trucks and increases travel time which increases transaction costs (in terms of time and money).

triples.subject: fertilizer_markets

triples.subject: consumption_data_from_dealers_or_farmers
triples.source_sentence: Ideally, consumption should relate to the quantities actually used by farmers on crops. This concept is difficult to apply as it requires costly surveys which cannot be conducted regularly. Therefore, it is ruled out as a tool for measuring consumption, on a comprehensive, timely and regular basis.

triples.subject: retail_dealers
triples.source_sentence: In practice, the regular collection of sales data from retail dealers, particularly in large countries, is difficult. Their numbers are large and not all retailers keep a proper record of their sales.

triples.subject: dealer_reporting_forms
triples.source_sentence: Some countries have developed regulations and legislation concerning packaging, distribution, sale, quality, specifications, price, etc. for fertilizers. The maintenance of records of stocks and sales by the retailer is often included in the regulations. In this case, dealer reporting forms (see table 17) could be sent to the central agency at specified intervals.

triples.subject: consumption_data_from_manufacturers_and_sales_organizations
triples.source_sentence: In most countries, the consumption statistics are in fact the actual deliveries to agriculture by the manufacturers. The figures may not reflect accurately current consumption in agriculture due to stock changes, but they are reliable since the recording unit is the factory or the trading enterprise (whose numbers are generally small) and such units keep good records of their operations.

triples.subject: Stock levels
triples.source_sentence: It assumes that supply (availability) equals consumption. This concept has its merits. Production data are normally fairly accurate and reliable since manufacturers keep their records up-to-date and report to the central agency every month. Secondly, the number of manufacturers is normally not very large in any given country. The import and export data are also reliable. The only uncertainties are the opening and closing stocks.

triples.subject: VAT
triples.source_sentence: The most typical tax imposed on fertilizers is value-added tax (VAT) which can range anywhere from 15-20%. VAT is typically calculated as a tax rate (%) on the sales value of the fertilizer.

triples.subject: Phosphate rock
triples.source_sentence: It is a natural rock containing one or more calcium phosphate minerals of sufficient purity and quantity as to permit its use directly after grinding or after chemical processing in the manufacture of commercial phosphate fertilizers.

triples.subject: Monoammonium phosphate (MAP)

triples.subject: Other nitrogen & phosphates compounds
triples.source_sentence: Other nitrogen & phosphates compounds It can be produced as the result of a chemical reaction of nitric acid on phosphate rock, with or without added ammonia and/or phosphoric and/or sulfuric acid or between sulfuric acid and ammonia or by simple mechanical mixing or blending. Other NP compound may also include some AN grades with small amounts of phosphates.

Between 2010 and 2019, fertilizer prices in Nigeria remained relatively stable, enabling farmers to plan input purchases with some degree of predictability.

Beginning in 2019 - 2020, however, fertilizer price stability deteriorated sharply. Global supply chain disruptions triggered by the COVID-19 pandemic reduced import reliability, increased transportation costs, and introduced significant market volatility.

The situation worsened in 2022 with the Russia - Ukraine war. Both countries are major exporters of nitrogen, phosphate, and potash fertilizers, and the conflict triggered sanctions, export restrictions, and a surge in natural gas and energy prices. Since natural gas is a primary feedstock for synthetic nitrogen fertilizers, global fertilizer prices soared to historic highs in 2022. Prices for common fertilizer types such as urea, NPK 15-15-15, and NPK 20-10-10 more than doubled between 2021 and 2022.

Prices moderated somewhat in 2023 - 2024 as global supply chains stabilized and PFI interventions increased domestic blending, yet retail prices and fertilizer-to-crop price ratios remain significantly higher than pre-pandemic levels.

triples.subject: Tillage
triples.source_sentence: Tillage refers to the agricultural preparation of soil through mechanical agitation, including digging, stirring, and overturning. It's a key practice for planting crops, as it helps to aerate the soil, manage weeds, and incorporate organic matter. In addition, tillage operations are primarily performed with tractors equipped with disc/mouldboard ploughs, harrowers, and ridgers.

triples.subject: Borno State

triples.subject: Gombe State
triples.source_sentence: Gombe State experienced a mixed trend with some species like Clarias showing reductions, while others, such as Tilapia, saw fluctuations in quantities across the markets.

triples.subject: Katsina State
triples.source_sentence: In the Northwest, Katsina State primarily traded Catfish and Tilapia, with a notable rise in 2024. Fresh Tilapia reached 2,113 MT in 2024, up from 2,000 MT in 2023.

triples.subject: Kebbi State

triples.subject: Zamfara State

triples.subject: Anambra State

Smoked fish trade also saw declines in several markets, though some increases were observed in Otuocha for smoked Tilapia.

triples.subject: Akwa-Ibom

triples.subject: Cross River

triples.subject: Ekiti State
triples.source_sentence: South-West, Ekiti State saw fluctuating quantities of both fresh and smoked Clarias and Tilapia species. While fresh Clarias volumes dropped slightly from 2,467 MT in 2023 to 1,948 MT in 2024, the smoked quantities slightly increased.

triples.subject: MTRM
triples.source_sentence: In 2024, record of MTRM shows that only Taraba (3), Gombe (4), Bayelsa (3), Edo (4), Rivers (3) and Ekiti (5) conducted MTRM. The record showed that there was low dissemination of improved agricultural technologies in the year under review.

triples.subject: FNT
triples.source_sentence: FNT is supposed to be conducted for about 26 times in a year but only Akwaibom (17), Bayelsa (3), Edo (14), Rivers (12), Ekiti (8), Ondo (16) and Osun (18) were able to conduct below 20 FNT in 2024. Over Fifty percent (50%) of the States did not conduct FNT in 2024. This implies that there was a big gap between the National Agricultural Research Institutes (NARIs) and the ADPs thereby, making frontline extension workers not to have access to new research technologies.

triples.subject: SPAT
triples.source_sentence: SPAT information reveals the following: Benue (70), Ekiti (50,000), Adamawa (165), Katsina (200), Akwaibom (680), Bayelsa (112) Edo (5671), Ondo (170), and Osun (24). Information on number of MTPs established across each state indicates Benue (105), Akwaibom (30), Rivers (3), Ondo (8) and Osun (2). Also, some states (Kogi, FCT, Kwara, Nasarawa, Plateau, Taraba, Kano and Enugu) had no report on OFAR, MTP and SPAT in 2024. The data provided revealed a slight decline in the activities compared to previous years. This implies that there was poor technology dissemination delivery in 2024.

triples.subject: Nigeria
triples.source_sentence: Nigeria is the largest producer of cowpea in the world and one of the highest consumers. This paper documents the challenges in cowpea production and consumption, export, and import trends in Nigeria. The critical and comparative review reveals several important insights. Cowpea is important for households and communities due to its substantial contributions to food security, nutrition, and revenue production. It plays a pivotal role in supporting various stakeholders involved in the value chain, including producers, processors, traders, and food vendors. Thus, cowpea is a crucial multipurpose crop. Although Nigeria is the largest producer of cowpea in the world, with a total production of 3.6 million tons in 2021, the demand for cowpea surpasses its supply due to factors such as the country's large population and low productivity.

triples.subject: Nigeria
triples.source_sentence: The Presidential Livestock Reforms Implementation Committee projections are unambiguous about the scale of transformation required. By 2050, Nigeria's population is projected to reach approximately 400 million, generating demand increases above current production levels of about 250 percent for poultry meat, 115 percent for beef, and 575 percent for milk (PLRIC 2025, NPC 2021, UN DESA 2022). Under a business-as-usual scenario, without targeted investment in productivity, processing, and market development, demand will outpace domestic supply growth, progressively deepening Nigeria's dependence on imports of livestock products. The direction of this trajectory is already observable in the dairy import bill of almost USD 300 million and growing feed import dependency, estimated at USD 50 million in 2025 (USDA-FAS 2025b, 2026).
